title: Survival
topic: Survival skills, equipment and natural disasters

slides.hook: If you got lost in a forest with only a rope, a torch and a whistle, what would you do first?

p: Things that are always true – facts of survival!
ex: If you **heat** water in a metal pot, it **boils**.
If you **don't drink** water in the heat, you **get** dehydrated.
If you **point** a magnifying glass at the sun, it **can start** a fire.

p: A real possibility in the future.
ex: If it **rains**, we**'ll put up** the tarpaulin.
We **won't find** the camp if we **don't take** a compass.

p: An imaginary or unlikely situation in the present or future.
With 'be', we often use 'were' for all persons: If I were you...
ex: If I **were** on a desert island, I**'d build** a shelter with rope and a tarpaulin.
If we **had** matches, we **could make** a fire.
**If I were you**, I'd put the phone in a waterproof bag.

p: 'Unless' means 'except if'. Don't use a negative verb after it.
ex: You'll get cold **unless** you **protect** yourself from the wind. (= if you don't protect)
**Unless** we **find** a source of clean water, we won't survive.

slides.title: What to do in an earthquake
text: If the ground **starts** to shake, **get** under a strong table. If you **are** outside, **move** away from buildings.
Keep a first-aid kit and a torch at home. If there **is** an earthquake at night, you**'ll need** them.
Don't use the lift **unless** it **is** safe. And remember: if everyone **stayed** calm, fewer people **would get** hurt.

items: If there will be an earthquake, get under a table.
If there is an earthquake, get under a table.
If I would have a compass, I'd know the way.
If I had a compass, I'd know the way.
Unless you don't take water, you'll get thirsty.
Unless you take water, you'll get thirsty.

grammar.title: Third conditional, I wish / If only
grammar.short: Imagining the past and expressing regrets

slides.hook: Think of a disaster you know about (a hurricane, a forest fire, a volcanic eruption). What could people have done differently?

rows: If they had checked the forecast,
they wouldn't have been caught in the avalanche.
If we had taken a compass,
we could have found the path.
slides.note: It's about an imaginary past: the opposite of what really happened.

p: Reality: They didn't bring a torch, so they got lost in the dark.
Imaginary past: If they **had brought** a torch, they **wouldn't have got** lost.
ex: If the alarm **had worked**, people **would have left** before the flooding.
She **might have survived** the hurricane if she **had stayed** inside.

p: We use 'What if...?' to imagine possible situations, past or future.
ex: **What if** the volcanic eruption starts tonight?
**What if** we **hadn't packed** the first-aid kit?

rows: I wish I had a torch. (I don't)
If only we had brought the water purification tablets!
I wish you would stop complaining about the heat!

slides.title: Lost in the mountains
text: Two hikers got lost in the Pyrenees last winter. 'If only we **had checked** the weather!' says Pablo. 'If we **had seen** the forecast, we **wouldn't have gone** up.'
Luckily, they had a whistle and a compass. 'If we **hadn't had** the whistle, the rescue team **wouldn't have found** us.'
'Now I wish I **knew** more about first aid. What if one of us **had been** injured?'

items: If I would have known about the flooding, I would have left.
If I had known about the flooding, I would have left.
Past perfect in the if clause.
I wish I have more water.
I wish I had more water.
If only I didn't forget the matches yesterday.
If only I hadn't forgotten the matches yesterday.

slides.q: If we ___ the forecast, we wouldn't have been caught in the avalanche.
It's so dark. I wish I ___ a torch.
slides.e: Wish about the present → past simple.

p: Third conditional: if + had done, would have done.
wish / if only + past simple → present.
wish / if only + past perfect → past regrets.
